description:
Delete the user and system `config.toml` layers, which no longer feed any configuration key, together with the `config set --global` write path that targets them.

## Background

Lease policy now resolves from the repository configuration only, through one resolver that `claim acquire` and the config commands share. That resolver was the only reader of the user (`~/.config/jit/config.toml`) and system (`/etc/jit/config.toml`) layers, so nothing reads those files any more. What remains is dead surface:

- `config set --global` writes the user-global file through the user-config store (`crates/jit/src/storage/user_config_store.rs`, called from `commands/config.rs`).
- CLI help and the configuration reference still describe user and system configuration files and a global scope.
- Any remaining loader, path resolution or test fixture that names those files.

The agent identity file `~/.config/jit/agent.toml` is a separate mechanism that the agent-id resolver reads; it stays.

## Success Criteria

- [hard] REQ-01: `config set` has no global scope: the `--global` flag and its dispatch are removed, and the user-config store's write path is deleted unless something else uses it.
- [hard] REQ-02: No code reads or resolves `~/.config/jit/config.toml` or `/etc/jit/config.toml`.
- [hard] REQ-03: The configuration reference's file table lists only repository-level files and the environment, and CLI help and docs describe no user or system configuration layer.
- [hard] REQ-04: A test proves that a `~/.config/jit/config.toml` present in the user's home has no effect on any configuration value or command.

## Notes

`~/.config/jit/agent.toml` is out of scope and keeps working. Removing a CLI flag changes the command schema: regenerate any projected CLI reference, and update MCP curated tools if a generated tool changes. Run the failure-corpus suite if a command's failure changes.
title: Remove the user and system configuration layers
